title: Celeriac Rémoulade with Mustard, Lemon and Parsley
summary: A French bistro classic of finely shredded celeriac in a creamy, lemony mustard dressing, lifted with fresh parsley and chives.
equipment: food processor with grating disc or julienne peeler

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, for wilting

steps.title: Prep the celeriac
steps.text: Slice the top and base off the celeriac, then cut away the knobbly skin following its curve, trimming off any stubborn brown bits with a small knife. Quarter it and shred into fine matchsticks using a food processor's grating disc or a julienne peeler. Cutting it this way, rather than grating finely, gives the rémoulade a pleasant bite instead of turning to mush.

steps.title: Wilt the celeriac
steps.text: Toss the shredded celeriac with the salt and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice in a colander, then leave it for 20-30 minutes. The salt draws out moisture and softens the raw crunch slightly, while the lemon stops it browning. Squeeze it firmly in a clean tea towel, a handful at a time, to get rid of the excess liquid.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.text: Stir the mustard powder with the cold water in a small bowl and leave it for 10 minutes to let its heat develop fully. Mix in the mayonnaise, yoghurt, lemon juice and pepper until smooth - the dressing should be a touch looser than plain mayonnaise, so add a teaspoon more water if it feels thick. Letting the mustard powder sit in water first brings out more flavour than adding it dry.

steps.title: Dress and chill
steps.text: Toss the squeezed celeriac with the dressing and most of the parsley and chives, then taste and adjust the salt and lemon to your liking. Chill for 1 hour before serving, as the flavours mellow and the texture turns pleasantly tender in that time. Scatter the remaining herbs over the top just before bringing it to the table.

tips: Squeeze the celeriac really firmly after wilting - leftover water will make the dressing watery and dull.
A common mistake is skipping the mustard powder's soaking time; give it the full 10 minutes in water so its flavour comes through properly.
Choose a celeriac that feels heavy and firm, as a soft or hollow one won't shred cleanly into crisp strands.
Chill the rémoulade for the full hour if you can - it tastes noticeably better once the flavours have had time to settle.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days; the celeriac will soften slightly but stays good to eat. This salad isn't suitable for freezing, as the mayonnaise and yoghurt will separate. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
